summary: access shutdown drains only already-arrived consumer errors; a failure during teardown still exits 0
description:
Deferred from TKT-98 ai-review pass 2 (finding R3, [high] as reported, triaged incidental). PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by TKT-98 -- verified against origin/main.

On SIGTERM, `awaitShutdown` (services/access/cmd/access/main.go) drains `consumerErr` for errors that have ALREADY arrived, then shuts the HTTP server down and returns. On the common path both consumer goroutines are still unwinding at that instant, so the channel is empty, the drain finds nothing, and any genuine consumer failure that materialises during teardown (durable deleted, subscription terminated, a NATS fault) is published to a channel nobody is reading any more. The process exits 0 while a consumer really did break.

Not a TKT-98 regression. Pre-fix, `origin/main`'s select had the same empty-channel state at SIGTERM, took the `ctx.Done()` branch, and returned `srv.Shutdown`'s nil result identically. TKT-98 neither introduced nor worsened this; it only removed the coin flip on errors that HAD already arrived. The code comment at the drain states the residual explicitly.

What closing it takes (the reviewer's recommendation, and why it is its own ticket): collect one terminal result from EACH consumer within a bounded grace period after cancellation, rather than snapshotting a shared channel. That is explicit consumer-lifecycle coordination -- `awaitShutdown` would have to know how many producers exist and wait on them, and every shutdown would then carry a grace period a wedged consumer can burn.

The trade to decide at shaping time: how much should an operator-requested stop pay, in shutdown latency and in lifecycle coupling, to report a consumer failure it noticed on the way out? A defensible answer is "nothing" -- in which case this ticket closes as won't-fix WITH the reasoning recorded, which is worth more than an undocumented gap. Note the sibling constraint: whatever shape is chosen should also fit inventory (TKT-121), or the two services drift.

Test note: any fix needs a delayed-send test -- a producer that sends only AFTER awaitShutdown has entered its drain. TKT-98's tests queue values before the call and by construction cannot express this.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from TKT-98's SECOND ai-review pass (gpt-5.6-sol), finding R3, reported [high] and triaged **incidental** on the ground that it is pre-existing and out of TKT-98's scope -- TKT-98 is "a clean shutdown must not report a consumer error", not "a shutdown must detect consumer errors", which is a capability the service has never had.

The pre-existing claim is verified, not asserted: `git show origin/main:services/access/cmd/access/main.go` shows the same select reaching `ctx.Done()` with an empty `consumerErr` and returning `srv.Shutdown`'s nil.

Recording the disagreement honestly: the reviewer rated this **high** and said "do not ship". It shipped, with the residual documented at the call site and here. If that judgement was wrong, this ticket is where it gets corrected -- which is the point of filing it rather than only rejecting it.

Needs shaping (COS + the 8-item DoR) before Gate 1.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Corroborated from inventory — TKT-121's ai-review re-flagged this window, independently, at `[high]`

TKT-121 shipped inventory's `awaitShutdown` (merged `2fb5709`). Its adversarial review
(`gpt-5.6-sol`, given the diff without the plan) found this same teardown window in inventory and
returned **"Do not ship"** on it, unprompted and without having seen TKT-122 or TKT-98's R3:

> After `ctx.Done()` wins, the code checks `consumerErr` only once and immediately proceeds to
> clean shutdown if the producer has not sent yet. A single producer limits cardinality, not
> timing […] A deterministic counterexample is an empty `consumerErr` followed by an error sent
> from the shutdown callback; the current function returns nil.

It arrived at the same recommendation this ticket already records (a bounded grace wait rather than
a zero-time snapshot) and at the same test note (a delayed-send producer, which neither service's
prequeued table can express).

**What this changes for TKT-122: nothing about its scope, something about its priority.** Two
independent adversarial reviews, on two services, months apart, both rating it `[high]` on first
sight is the strongest signal available that the gap is not obvious-in-hindsight — it is what a
fresh reader concludes. The counter-argument stays exactly as this ticket already states it: the
process is stopping on operator request, and the cost of closing the window is a shutdown a wedged
consumer can delay.

**Inventory is now confirmed to have the identical window**, so this ticket's "should also fit
inventory (TKT-121), or the two services drift" is no longer forward-looking — both services are in
the state, and both `awaitShutdown` implementations would change together. Inventory's version
takes ONE non-blocking receive rather than access's drain loop (single producer, buffered-1
channel), so a bounded-wait design has to work for both cardinalities.

TKT-121 left a comment on inventory's test at the `real failure landing during shutdown` case
naming this window as uncovered and pointing here, so the boundary is visible from the test rather
than only from the board.
